content.comment_body: Has anyone managed to get this working? My current setup is: 1) [product_name] panel connected to [product_name] module – works fine using an S7-200 type connector. 2) [version_no] acting as server, [product_name] as client – works fine. 3) [product_name] RT Advanced: a) [version_no] – successfully reads values from the [product_name] module. b) [product_name] module – not working. I’ve tried both S7-200 and [product_name] connectors, but it’s still not working. Any suggestions?
Hello, Are all the listed devices on the same subnet? If so, why not use the [version_no] to read values from the [product_name] module and act as a gateway?

Thank you for the quick response. Yes, that’s basically the commercial solution we’re running. My broader question is whether anyone else has faced this issue and found a solution, ideally before I start using a network analyzer for further troubleshooting. Has it worked previously and is now failing? Also, it seems that emulating a Basic Panel doesn't work either.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter unreliable communication when connecting [product_name] module directly to [product_name] RT Advanced. While connections via [product_name] panel and [version_no] are stable, direct communication is problematic. Routing data through the [version_no] works, indicating possible compatibility or feature limitations between the [product_name] module and [product_name] RT Advanced.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek reliable, direct, and officially supported communication between the [product_name] module and [product_name] RT Advanced, hoping for the same seamless integration found with other hardware and panels from [company_name].
